amc8-ajhsme-1992-02.title: Decimals
amc8-ajhsme-1992-02.body:
$\frac54=1.25$. The choices are $1.25, 1.25, 1.25, 1.2, 1.25$. Only $1\frac15=1.2$ is different.

**Answer: (D) $1\dfrac{1}{5}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-03.title: Largest minus smallest
amc8-ajhsme-1992-03.body:
To make $a-b$ as large as possible, take $a$ largest and $b$ smallest: $12-(-16)=28$.

**Answer: (D) 28**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-03.title: Number line
amc8-ajhsme-1992-03.body:
The difference is the distance from $b$ up to $a$. The farthest apart numbers are $-16$ and $12$, which are $28$ apart.

**Answer: (D) 28**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-04.title: Non-singles
amc8-ajhsme-1992-04.body:
$7$ of $35$ hits were not singles, which is $\frac15=20\%$. So $80\%$ were singles.

**Answer: (E) $80\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-05.title: Subtract the circle
amc8-ajhsme-1992-05.body:
Rectangle: $6$. Circle of radius $\frac12$: $\pi\cdot\frac14\approx0.79$. Shaded $\approx6-0.79=5.21$, closest to $5$.

**Answer: (E) 5**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-05.title: Estimate
amc8-ajhsme-1992-05.body:
The circle fits inside a $1\times1$ square, so it has area less than $1$ but more than half of $1$. The shaded area is between $5$ and $5.5$: closest to $5$.

**Answer: (E) 5**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-07.title: List them
amc8-ajhsme-1992-07.body:
Three digits adding to $26$ must be $9,9,8$ (the most is $27$). The numbers are $998, 989, 899$. Only $998$ is even: $1$ number.

**Answer: (A) 1**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-07.title: Last digit
amc8-ajhsme-1992-07.body:
An even number with digit sum $26$ needs an even last digit. The last digit must be at least $26-18=8$, so it is $8$, and the other two are $9,9$: only $998$.

**Answer: (A) 1**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-08.title: Revenue needed
amc8-ajhsme-1992-08.body:
Cost: $1500\times\$0.10=\$150$. For a $\$100$ profit he needs $\$250$ of sales, which is $250\div0.25=1000$ pencils.

**Answer: (C) 1000**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-08.title: Check the answer
amc8-ajhsme-1992-08.body:
Selling $1000$ pencils brings in $\$250$; minus the $\$150$ cost leaves exactly $\$100$.

**Answer: (C) 1000**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-09.title: Compare the bars
amc8-ajhsme-1992-09.body:
The F bar is twice as tall as the M bar (two equal blocks vs one). So females : males $=2:1$, and males are $\frac13$ of $480$: $160$.

**Answer: (B) 160**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-09.title: Blocks
amc8-ajhsme-1992-09.body:
There are $3$ equal blocks in all ($2$ for F, $1$ for M), each standing for $480\div3=160$ people. Males: $160$.

**Answer: (B) 160**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-10.title: Area per small triangle
amc8-ajhsme-1992-10.body:
The big triangle has area $\frac12\cdot8\cdot8=32$, so each small triangle has area $\frac{32}{16}=2$. Counting shaded triangles row by row: $4+3+2+1=10$. Shaded area $=10\times2=20$.

**Answer: (B) 20**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-10.title: Fraction shaded
amc8-ajhsme-1992-10.body:
The shaded triangles are $10$ of the $16$ (the ones pointing the same way as the big triangle), so the area is $\frac{10}{16}\times32=20$.

**Answer: (B) 20**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-11.title: Read the bars
amc8-ajhsme-1992-11.body:
Frequencies: red $50$, blue $60$, brown $40$, pink $60$, green $40$. Total $250$. Blue: $\frac{60}{250}=\frac{24}{100}=24\%$.

**Answer: (B) $24\%$**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-12.title: Tire-miles
amc8-ajhsme-1992-12.body:
At every moment $4$ tires are on the road, so there are $4\times30{,}000=120{,}000$ tire-miles in total. Shared equally among $5$ tires: $24{,}000$ miles each.

**Answer: (C) 24,000**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-12.title: Fraction of the time
amc8-ajhsme-1992-12.body:
Each tire is resting $\frac15$ of the time and on the road $\frac45$ of the time: $\frac45\times30{,}000=24{,}000$.

**Answer: (C) 24,000**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-13.title: Build the list
amc8-ajhsme-1992-13.body:
In order the scores are $a\le b\le 91\le d\le e$. The mode $94$ must appear at least twice, and only $d,e$ can be $94$. So $d=e=94$. The total is $5\times90=450$, so $a+b=450-91-94-94=171$.

**Answer: (B) 171**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-13.title: Try an example
amc8-ajhsme-1992-13.body:
The scores $85, 86, 91, 94, 94$ have mean $90$, median $91$ and mode $94$; their two lowest add to $171$. The first method shows every such list gives the same sum, so the answer is determined: $171$.

**Answer: (B) 171**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-14.title: Difference of fractions
amc8-ajhsme-1992-14.body:
The $4$ gallons fill $\frac12-\frac13=\frac16$ of the tank. So the whole tank holds $6\times4=24$ gallons.

**Answer: (D) 24**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-14.title: Check
amc8-ajhsme-1992-14.body:
A $24$-gallon tank one-third full holds $8$ gallons; adding $4$ gives $12$, which is half. ✓

**Answer: (D) 24**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-15.title: Find the period
amc8-ajhsme-1992-15.body:
The block $\text{ABCDEDCBA}$ of $9$ letters repeats. $1992=9\times221+3$, so the $1992$nd letter is the $3$rd letter of a block: C.

**Answer: (C) C**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-15.title: Use a nearby multiple
amc8-ajhsme-1992-15.body:
Letter $1989$ ($=9\times221$) is the last A of a block. Letters $1990, 1991, 1992$ are A, B, C.

**Answer: (C) C**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-16.title: Scaling
amc8-ajhsme-1992-16.body:
Doubling the height doubles the volume; doubling the radius multiplies it by $4$. Choice (B) keeps the radius and doubles the height.

**Answer: (B)**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-17.title: Triangle inequality
amc8-ajhsme-1992-17.body:
The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest: $6.5+s>10$, so $s>3.5$. The smallest whole number is $4$.

**Answer: (B) 4**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-17.title: Test s = 3
amc8-ajhsme-1992-17.body:
With $s=3$: $6.5+3=9.5<10$, so the sides can't close up into a triangle. With $s=4$: $10.5>10$ works.

**Answer: (B) 4**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-18.title: Total distance over total time
amc8-ajhsme-1992-18.body:
Distance $80+100=180$ miles; time $1.5+0.5+2=4$ hours. Average speed $=\frac{180}{4}=45$ mph.

**Answer: (A) 45**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-18.title: Don't average the speeds
amc8-ajhsme-1992-18.body:
The two moving speeds were about $53$ and $50$ mph, but the $30$-minute stop counts as part of the trip time. Only total distance $\div$ total time counts: $180\div4=45$.

**Answer: (A) 45**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-19.title: Make the other gaps small
amc8-ajhsme-1992-19.body:
From exit $5$ to exit $26$ there are $21$ gaps between consecutive exits. Make $20$ of them as short as allowed, $5$ miles each: $100$ miles. The remaining gap is $118-100=18$ miles.

**Answer: (C) 18**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-19.title: Check
amc8-ajhsme-1992-19.body:
Twenty gaps of $5$ and one of $18$: $20\times5+18=118$ ✓. Any longer gap would force another gap below $5$ miles.

**Answer: (C) 18**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-20.title: Fold pattern D
amc8-ajhsme-1992-20.body:
In (D), take the middle square of the vertical column of three as the bottom. The squares above and below it become the back and front faces, and the square to its left becomes the left face. The square attached to the right of the front face becomes the right face, and the last square, attached to the right of that, folds up onto the back, which is already covered. Two squares overlap and the top is missing, so (D) cannot form a cube.

**Answer: (D)**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-20.title: Check the others
amc8-ajhsme-1992-20.body:
(A) is a staircase of three pairs, a standard cube net. (B), (C) and (E) each have a row of four squares with one square above the row and one below it: the row wraps around to make four sides of the cube and the other two squares close the top and bottom. Only (D) fails.

**Answer: (D)**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-21.title: Compute each percent
amc8-ajhsme-1992-21.body:
(Drums, bugles) by month: Jan $(7,9)$, Feb $(5,3)$, Mar $(9,6)$, Apr $(9,12)$, May $(8,10)$. The larger exceeds the smaller by (as a percent of the smaller): Jan $\frac27\approx29\%$, Feb $\frac23\approx67\%$, Mar $\frac36=50\%$, Apr $\frac39\approx33\%$, May $\frac28=25\%$. The largest is February.

**Answer: (B) Feb**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-21.title: Compare ratios
amc8-ajhsme-1992-21.body:
The ratios larger : smaller are $\frac97, \frac53, \frac96, \frac{12}{9}, \frac{10}{8}$, i.e. about $1.29, 1.67, 1.5, 1.33, 1.25$. February's $\frac53$ is largest.

**Answer: (B) Feb**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-22.title: How much can each tile add?
amc8-ajhsme-1992-22.body:
A new tile has $4$ sides. If it shares $k$ sides with the figure, the perimeter changes by $4-2k$. Since $k\ge1$, each tile adds at most $2$, so the new perimeter is at most $14+2+2=18$. And $18$ happens: put one tile to the left of the bottom row and one to the right of the top row; each touches only one side.

**Answer: (C) 18**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-22.title: Parity
amc8-ajhsme-1992-22.body:
Each change $4-2k$ is even, so the perimeter stays even: $15, 17, 19$ are impossible, and $20$ is more than the maximum $18$. So the answer must be $18$ (and it is achievable).

**Answer: (C) 18**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-23.title: Count products at most 10
amc8-ajhsme-1992-23.body:
For first die $1,2,3,4,5,6$, the second die values giving product $\le10$ number $6,5,3,2,2,1$: $19$ outcomes. So $36-19=17$ outcomes give a product greater than $10$: probability $\frac{17}{36}$.

**Answer: (B) $\dfrac{17}{36}$**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-24.title: Square minus quarter circles
amc8-ajhsme-1992-24.body:
The square joining the centers has side $6$ and area $36$. Inside it, each circle contributes a quarter circle; the four quarters make one full circle of area $9\pi\approx28.27$. Shaded area $\approx36-28.27=7.73$, closest to $7.7$.

**Answer: (A) 7.7**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-24.title: Estimate
amc8-ajhsme-1992-24.body:
$\pi\approx3.14$ gives $36-28.3\approx7.7$; using $\pi\approx3$ gives $9$, so (A) is the only sensible choice.

**Answer: (A) 7.7**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-25.title: Telescoping product
amc8-ajhsme-1992-25.body:
After $n$ pourings the remaining fraction is $\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdot\frac34\cdots\frac{n}{n+1}=\frac{1}{n+1}$. This equals $\frac1{10}$ when $n=9$.

**Answer: (D) 9**

amc8-ajhsme-1992-25.title: Watch the pattern
amc8-ajhsme-1992-25.body:
After pouring 1: $\frac12$; 2: $\frac12\cdot\frac23=\frac13$; 3: $\frac13\cdot\frac34=\frac14$; ... each pouring makes it $\frac{1}{\text{next number}}$. After $9$ pourings: $\frac1{10}$.

**Answer: (D) 9**
